s.note: Annie works the late shift at the diner while Hogarth hides a giant
s.how: Clams, potato and smoky bacon in a creamy broth, served in mugs with crackers. Fry 4 rashers diced bacon until crisp, add 1 diced onion and 2 diced celery sticks and soften. Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 500ml fish stock, 400g diced potatoes and a bay leaf and simmer 15 minutes. Add 1kg vongole, cover and cook 5 minutes until they open, then pull most of the meat from the shells. Stir in 250ml cream, warm through, season and serve with crackers.

s.note: The government man from Washington, who moves into Hogarth's spare room
s.how: Hard-boiled eggs filled with a creamy mustard yolk, piped high and dusted with paprika and chives. Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool in iced water and peel. Halve and mash the yolks with 4 tbsp mayonnaise, 2 tsp Dijon mustard, 1 tsp white vinegar, salt and pepper. Pipe or spoon back into the whites, dust with smoked paprika and scatter with snipped chives.

m.note: Beef and pork meatloaf with tomato glaze, served with mash and peas
m.how: Mix 500g beef mince, 300g pork mince, 60g breadcrumbs, 1 egg and 1 grated onion with salt and pepper. Shape in a tin, glaze with 80ml tomato sauce and bake at 180C for 60 minutes. Serve thick slices with 1kg potatoes mashed with butter and 300g peas.

w.note: Crunchy peanut brittle broken into jagged shards, brushed with edible silver
w.how: Line a tray with baking paper. Heat 300g caster sugar, 120ml liquid glucose and 80ml water in a heavy pan to 150C on a sugar thermometer. Take off the heat and quickly stir in 250g roasted peanuts, 20g butter and 1 tsp bicarb soda. Pour onto the tray and spread thin. Sprinkle with flaky salt and brush lightly with silver edible lustre. Cool 30 minutes, then smash into jagged shards.

d.note: Espresso, vanilla ice cream and malt blended thick, topped with whipped cream
d.how: Brew 2 shots espresso and cool, or use decaf for younger kids. Blend with 8 scoops vanilla ice cream, 400ml cold milk and 3 tbsp malted milk powder for 30 seconds until thick. Pour into 4 tall glasses. Top each with whipped cream and a few chocolate-coated coffee beans, or chocolate sprinkles for the little ones.
